bibleSpine.kjv: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
bibleSpine.gloss: The charter promise of the section: sin SHALL NOT rule the believer — stated as a future certainty, not a wish. Grace, not law-under-condemnation, is the ground of the deliverance.

bibleSpine.kjv: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: The mechanism of 6:14: the old man crucified with Christ so the body of sin is destroyed — provision that we 'should not serve sin.' Victory is by union with the crucified Christ, not by native effort.

bibleSpine.kjv: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'Made free from sin' — the freedom is present and actual, bearing fruit unto holiness. The gospel result is not managed failure but genuine liberty from sin's service.

bibleSpine.kjv: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.
bibleSpine.gloss: The new-birth life 'doth not commit sin' and 'cannot sin' — because the divine seed remains. Not sinlessness in the flesh apart from Christ, but the born-of-God nature that does not practise sin while it abides in Him.

bibleSpine.kjv: He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ was manifested to DESTROY the works of the devil — sin itself — in the believer. The purpose of the incarnation is the undoing of sin, not its accommodation.

bibleSpine.kjv: For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.
bibleSpine.gloss: Defines the overcomer: whatsoever is born of God OVERCOMETH — and names the means, 'even our faith.' The same faith is 'the victory,' the identical victory by which Christ overcame (Rev. 3:21).

bibleSpine.kjv: We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not.
bibleSpine.gloss: The born-of-God one 'sinneth not' and 'that wicked one toucheth him not' — kept, guarded, untouched. The overcomer's security is real, not aspirational.

bibleSpine.kjv: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,
bibleSpine.gloss: God is ABLE to keep you from falling and to present you faultless. The keeping power and the faultless standing are both His work — falling is never made necessary.

bibleSpine.kjv: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
bibleSpine.gloss: With EVERY temptation God makes a way to escape — so no temptation ever compels sin. The escape is guaranteed by God's faithfulness; sin is therefore always avoidable.

bibleSpine.kjv: Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
bibleSpine.gloss: God ALWAYS causeth us to triumph in Christ — 'always,' with no exception clause for necessary defeat. Triumph, not managed failure, is the standing gospel norm.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
bibleSpine.gloss: The grace is SUFFICIENT — provision is complete, matched precisely to weakness. His strength is perfected exactly where we are weakest, so no infirmity is an excuse for sin.

bibleSpine.kjv: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'All things' — the compass of the provision. Nothing God requires lies outside the enabling of the indwelling Christ.

bibleSpine.kjv: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ was tempted 'in all points like as we are, YET WITHOUT SIN' — proving that being tempted, even in our infirmities, never made sinning inevitable. He met temptation on our ground and did not fall.

bibleSpine.kjv: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
bibleSpine.gloss: The capstone: the promise is to him that overcometh EVEN AS I ALSO OVERCAME — the same victory, held to the same standard, by the same faith, in the same flesh. Christ's overcoming is the pattern, not an exception.

bibleSpine.kjv: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.
bibleSpine.gloss: Every church-letter reward is conditioned 'to him that overcometh' — the overcomer is the assumed normal Christian, and Eden restored is his inheritance.

bibleSpine.kjv: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'He shall go no more out' — the overcomer's final settled security. The reiterated 'him that overcometh' fixes overcoming as the condition Christ everywhere expects and enables.

bibleSpine.kjv: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous:
bibleSpine.gloss: The aim is stated plainly — 'that ye sin not.' The Advocate is the provision for the one who DOES fall, but the 'if' guards the mark: falling is possible, never necessary; the standard is never lowered to it.

bibleSpine.kjv: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
bibleSpine.gloss: His very name declares the errand: to save His people FROM their sins, not merely from sin's penalty in them. Salvation that leaves sin reigning would contradict the name Jesus.

bibleSpine.kjv: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
bibleSpine.gloss: He gave Himself to redeem us from ALL iniquity and to purify a people — the redemption's design is complete cleansing, not partial. No known sin need be retained.

symbolDefs.meaning: One in whom the born-of-God life triumphs over sin and the world — not by native strength but by Christ living out in fallen flesh the very victory He Himself won. Scripture defines it: 'whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world' and the means is 'even our faith' (1 John 5:4) — the same faith Christ exercised; 'begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not' (1 John 5:18); the reward is 'to him that overcometh... even as I also overcame' (Rev. 3:21), the identical victory; and the life is 'not I, but Christ liveth in me' (Gal. 2:20). The overcomer is thus the normal Christian of Revelation's promises (2:7; 3:12), one 'made free from sin' (Rom. 6:22) over whom sin 'shall not have dominion' (Rom. 6:14).
receipts: 1 John 5:4 — 'whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith' — overcoming defined, and its means named as faith
1 John 5:18 — 'he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not' — the overcomer kept and untouched
Revelation 3:21 — 'to him that overcometh... even as I also overcame' — the SAME victory Christ won is the pattern for the overcomer
Galatians 2:20 — 'nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me' — the overcoming is Christ living out His own victory in the believer's flesh
Romans 6:14 — 'sin shall not have dominion over you' — the overcomer's charter: sin dethroned
Romans 6:22 — 'being made free from sin' — the overcomer's actual present freedom
Revelation 2:7; 3:12 — the reward promised 'to him that overcometh' — overcoming is the assumed condition of every church

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: A questioner may say, "You make it out that we ought never to sin any more, - you leave no room for sin." But is not that what the Bible says? "For sin shall not have dominion over you; for ye are not under the law, but under grace." ... There is such a thing as a complete surrender to Christ, - when we give up everything, and then trust to his power to keep us in that state. And I thank God that he is able to do it.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner meets the exact objection of this section head-on — must we always fall short? — and answers from Rom. 6:14 itself: no, we ought never to sin any more, and Christ 'is able' to keep us there. Direct confirmation that provision is complete.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: Sin has no dominion over those who yield themselves servants to righteousness, or to obedience to the law; because sin is the transgression of the law. Now read the whole of the fourteenth verse: "For sin shall not have dominion over you; for ye are not under the law, but under grace." That is to say, transgression of the law has no place in them who are not under the law.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner's exposition of Rom. 6:14 confirming the symbol: 'transgression of the law has no place' in the one under grace. Sin's dominion is actually broken, not merely re-labeled.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: And this faith of Jesus, by which in the place of the lost, He hoped in God and trusted God for salvation from sin and power to keep from sinning—this victory of His it is that has brought to every man in the world divine faith by which every man can... find the power of God to deliver him from sin and to keep him from sinning. That faith which He exercised and by which He obtained the victory over the world, the flesh, and the devil—that faith is His free gift to every lost man in the world. And thus "this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith."
witnesses.gloss: Jones defines the overcomer symbol exactly as Scripture does: Christ's own victory-faith, that same faith by which He overcame, is His free gift to every man — 'power to keep from sinning.' The same victory, by the same faith, quoting 1 John 5:4. Anchors Rev. 3:21 and the section's thesis.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: He says to them, "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect." And He says this because He knows that it is possible for them to reach perfection. He lived in this world the life that they must live. He met the foe single-handed, as they must meet him. He asked and received power to enable Him to overcome in the conflict. And those who walk in God's way may have the same power.... As He overcame, so we may overcome.
witnesses.gloss: Corroborates Rev. 3:21 word for word in principle: 'As He overcame, so we may overcome' by 'the same power' — and that God commands perfection 'because He knows that it is possible.' The mark is not lowered.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The question is, Shall we keep on sinning as though it were an impossibility for us to overcome? How are we to overcome? As Christ overcame, and that is the only way.... When tempted to speak wrong and do wrong resist Satan and say, I will not surrender my will to your control. I will cooperate with divine power and through grace be conqueror.
witnesses.gloss: Answers the section's central question directly — no, we need not keep on sinning; we overcome 'as Christ overcame, and that is the only way.' Ties the overcomer to the right action of the will co-operating with divine power.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: We need not place the obedience of Christ by itself as something for which He was particularly adapted, by His particular divine nature, for He stood before God as man's representative and tempted as man's substitute and surety. If Christ had a special power which it is not the privilege of man to have, Satan would have made capital of this matter.... a man, tempted as a man, rendering the obedience of a man.
witnesses.gloss: Guards the 'even as I also overcame' pillar: Christ overcame with no special power unavailable to us, as man's representative. Therefore His victory is genuinely reproducible — the same victory, in the same flesh.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: We shall all be tempted in a variety of ways, but when we are tempted we need to remember that a provision has been made whereby we may overcome.... He who truly believes in Christ is made partaker of the divine nature, and has power that he can appropriate under every temptation. He will not fall under temptation or be left to defeat.
witnesses.gloss: Corroborates 1 Cor. 10:13 and the completeness of provision: 'a provision has been made whereby we may overcome' every temptation — 'He will not fall.' Falling is never necessary.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When we are tempted, we need to remember that provision has been made whereby we may overcome.... He who truly believes in Christ is made a partaker of the divine nature, and has power that he can appropriate under every temptation. He will not fall under temptation, and be left to defeat. In time of trial he will claim the promises, and by these escape the corruptions that are in the world through lust.
witnesses.gloss: A second witness to the same truth from the Review: provision under EVERY temptation, 'he will not fall,' escaping by the promises — confirming 1 Cor. 10:13's guaranteed way of escape.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: What you need to understand is the true force of the will. This is the governing power in the nature of man, the power of decision, or of choice. Everything depends on the right action of the will.... You can give Him your will; He will then work in you to will and to do according to His good pleasure. Thus your whole nature will be brought under the control of the Spirit of Christ.
witnesses.gloss: The named EGW anchor on the will: the point where provision is appropriated. Victory is not passive — the believer yields the will, God works the doing. Confirms that no sin need be retained because the choice to serve God is always available.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Said the tried apostle Paul: "He said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness.... for when I am weak, then am I strong." 2 Corinthians 12:9, 10.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms 2 Cor. 12:9: the grace is sufficient and strength is perfected in weakness — the very infirmities that seem to excuse defeat are where Christ's power rests. Provision is matched to weakness.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Those who overcome as Christ overcame will need to constantly guard themselves against the temptations of Satan.... Many desire the final reward and victory which are to be given to overcomers, but are not willing to endure toil, privation, and denial of self, as did their Redeemer. It is only through obedience and continual effort that we shall overcome as Christ overcame.
witnesses.gloss: Corroborates Rev. 3:21 and defines the overcomer's path: 'overcome as Christ overcame' through obedience and continual effort. The victory is real and reproducible, but costly — not automatic, not lowered to managed failure.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Christ is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own.
witnesses.gloss: The standard-setting anchor: 'the character of Christ... perfectly reproduced' is the goal — the overcomer's completion. Confirms that complete victory (Christ's own character in His people) is exactly what God is waiting to accomplish, not an unreachable ideal.

historyAnchor: The pioneer witnesses cluster around the 1888 Minneapolis message and its aftermath (Waggoner's Romans lectures and Jones's later Consecrated Way, with EGW's 1891-1909 amplifications), when righteousness by faith and complete victory over sin were pressed on the Adventist church.
uncertainties: The candidate periodical statement 'The Lord requires nothing that we cannot render' (attributed in some compilations to RH Oct. 12, 1886, par. 15) was DROPPED: reading the full paragraph from the local database showed it does not contain that clause, so citing it would misattribute the quote.

1 John 3:9's 'cannot sin' is quoted verbatim; the section should present it as the pioneers/EGW resolve it — the born-of-God nature does not practise sin while abiding in Christ (not an inherent human sinlessness apart from Him) — consistent with 1 John 2:1 leaving room for a fall that is possible but never necessary.

EGW nature-of-Christ guard statements (e.g. FLB 49.4 / 5BC 1128, 'not for one moment was there in Him an evil propensity') were deliberately NOT cited here: they belong to the separate nature-of-Christ section and concern His consent/character, not this section's victory thesis.

The GTI/CHR search for a Waggoner 'even as I also overcame / same victory' statement returned nothing verbatim in the local corpus; the same-victory theme is instead carried by the verified CWCP 50.1 (Jones) and ST Jan. 8, 1902 (EGW), which is sufficient.
